title: The archer born of anger
hookLine: an old ritual book tells how Rudra was born of wrath, and how the gods calmed him with a hymn
carry: the rudram bows to anger, then asks for peace
tomorrow: who gets to see Shiva? the hymn names a cowherd.

cards: An old ritual book, the Shatapatha Brahmana, tells a frightening story. The creator, Prajapati, has fallen apart, worn out from making the world, and the gods have drifted away from him.

Only one power stays inside him: Manyu, wrath. Prajapati weeps, his tears settle on that wrath, and it becomes Rudra: a hundred heads, a thousand eyes, a hundred quivers of arrows. The gods are terrified.
What do you do with a god like that?

teach.b: The gods say to one another: let's gather food for him, and calm him. So they offer him the hymn of the hundred Rudras, the Shatarudriya, and with it, the story says, he is appeased.
That hymn is the Rudram, in the Krishna Yajur Veda.
Listen to its first line: namaste rudra manyave. A bow to your anger, Rudra. Manyu, the very wrath he was made from.
Then a bow to his arrow, his bow, his arms. It doesn't pretend the danger isn't there. It names it, and bows.
Make your arrow kind. Look on us with your auspicious body. Unstring the bow; put the arrows away.
The word for kind and auspicious there is shiva. So the hymn asks Rudra, in a sense, to be Shiva, and trusts the fierce one has a gentle face.

Here's the teaching, and a practice you can still watch: Hindus chant the Rudram at abhishekam, as water or milk is poured slowly over the Shiva linga, on Mondays, Shiva's day, and through the night of Shivaratri.

Many devotees speak of the pouring as cooling and soothing the fierce one, the way the gods once calmed him with the hymn. Facing anger, there are two easy moves: pretend it isn't there, or go to war with it.

teach.h: BOW TO IT, THEN ASK FOR PEACE.
teach.b: It bows, sees the anger fully, and from that bow asks for peace. The hymn says that works on a god. It's worth trying on a temper too, including your own.

how: Hindus chant the Shri Rudram in Sanskrit, often in Shiva temples during abhishekam, as water or milk is poured over the Shiva linga; some learn it by heart from a teacher, line by line.

games.q: you're one of the gods, facing an archer born of wrath, a hundred quivers at his side. what does the Rudram say first?
games.why: namaste rudra manyave: a bow to your anger, Rudra. see it fully, then ask for the kind face.

practice: Try a small abhishekam. If you have a Shiva linga or an image, pour a little water over it slowly; if not, pour water from one cup into another.
As it flows, let something that angers you come to mind, yours or someone else's, and see it clearly without fighting it. If you pray, say namaste rudra manyave, or Om namah shivaya.
If you don't, ask the anger, silently, for its kinder face.

wordCard.voice: The Rudram. A Vedic hymn offered to calm the archer born of wrath: it bows to his anger and asks him to be shiva, kind.
